places.title: La Borda
places.why: A cooperative housing block built on public land by its future residents: 28 homes in a timber structure around a large covered courtyard, with a shared kitchen, laundry and terraces.

places.architect: Josep Lluís Sert, Joan Baptista Subirana, Josep Torres Clavé (GATCPAC)
places.why: The manifesto of Catalan rationalism: workers' duplex flats along a continuous stepped block around shared gardens. One flat is kept as a museum.

photos.file: 363 Casa Bloc, pg. Torras i Bages 85-105 (Barcelona), façana dels jardins interiors.jpg

places.title: Montbau
places.architect: Guillermo Giráldez, Pedro López Íñigo, Xavier Subías, Antoni Bonet and others
places.why: A modern housing estate on the slopes of Collserola: slabs and towers set among pedestrian gardens, one of the best-preserved post-war neighbourhoods in the city.

photos.file: Centre Sociosanitari Sant Jordi Caixa Catalunya.jpg
photos.author: Joandrés

photos.author: Enfo

places.title: Torre Júlia
places.architect: Pau Vidal, Sergi Pons, Ricard Galiana
places.why: Public housing for older residents on the hillside of Nou Barris, winner of the Barcelona City Architecture Award 2011.

places.title: Apartment building for four friends
places.why: A small apartment building in Poblenou designed for four friends who share it, with common outdoor spaces.

photos.file: Edifici d'habitatges per a quatre amics (24571).jpg
photos.author: Cataleirxs

places.title: APROP Ciutat Vella
places.why: Temporary social housing built from reused shipping containers, stacked into a small courtyard building in the old town — quick to build and movable.

places.title: 85 social dwellings in Cornellà
places.why: Public housing with a timber structure and equal-sized rooms without corridors, so each flat can be used flexibly — a reference for low-carbon housing in Spain.

places.title: GREENH@USE — 140 social dwellings in 22@
places.why: Social housing in the 22@ innovation district built with an industrialised timber system and generous shared spaces; one of the 40 works shortlisted for the EUmies Awards 2026.

places.title: Edificio Caracol — 79 protected dwellings
places.why: Winner of the FAD Architecture Prize 2020: a block of 79 public dwellings nicknamed the Snail for its spiralling form, in the centre of Sant Boi.

places.title: Mercat de Santa Caterina
places.why: A 19th-century market under a wildly undulating roof of coloured ceramic hexagons that pixelate fruit and vegetables — best seen from the surrounding balconies.

places.title: Sagrada Família
places.why: Gaudí's basilica, still under construction: a forest of branching stone columns under a ceiling of light. The Nativity facade and the crypt are on the UNESCO list.

photos.author: Hetemacaba

places.title: Torre Glòries
places.architect: Jean Nouvel, b720 Fermín Vázquez Arquitectos
places.why: A rounded tower wrapped in coloured panels behind a veil of glass louvres that shimmers from red to blue — the landmark of the 22@ district.

places.why: Barcelona's historic flea market under a folded mirrored canopy that reflects the stalls below, next to Torre Glòries.

places.title: Edifici Fòrum (Museu Blau)
places.why: A floating blue triangle of textured concrete lifted over a shaded public plaza, now home to the Natural Sciences Museum.

places.title: El Born Centre de Cultura i Memòria
places.architect: Josep Fontserè (market); Enric Sòria, Rafael Cáceres (conversion); vora (surroundings)
places.why: A 19th-century iron market turned into a covered public square over the excavated streets of the 1714 city, with the surrounding streets reworked around it.

places.title: MACBA — Museu d'Art Contemporani
places.why: A white museum whose glass ramp hall faces a square that has become the city's skateboarding stage.

photos.author: Zarateman

places.title: Casa Batlló
places.why: Gaudí's remodelling of an Eixample house into a sea creature: bone-like balconies, a scaly roof and a light well tiled from deep to pale blue.

photos.file: Casa Batllo Overview Barcelona Spain cut.jpg
photos.author: ChristianSchd

places.title: Casa Milà (La Pedrera)
places.why: An undulating stone apartment block without load-bearing facade walls, crowned by a rooftop of sculpted chimneys and stair towers.

places.title: Palau de la Música Catalana
places.architect: Lluís Domènech i Montaner; extension by Óscar Tusquets
places.why: A modernista concert hall with walls almost entirely of glass and an inverted stained-glass dome hanging over the auditorium.

places.title: Casa Vicens
places.architect: Antoni Gaudí; restoration by Martínez Lapeña & Torres
places.why: Gaudí's first house: a Moorish-inspired villa of green-and-white tiles and brick, restored and opened as a museum in 2017.

places.title: Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau
places.why: A garden city of modernista hospital pavilions linked by underground tunnels, restored as a cultural and research campus.

places.title: Barcelona Pavilion
places.architect: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, Lilly Reich
places.why: The German pavilion of the 1929 Expo, rebuilt in 1986: free-standing planes of onyx, travertine and glass that defined modern open space.

places.why: A 19th-century water reservoir with a forest of tall brick arches, converted into a university library.

places.why: A library tucked under the garden of a historic villa, so the new building reads more as landscape than as volume.

places.title: Fort Pienc
places.why: A library, school, market and housing layered into one Eixample block around a public square.

places.title: Llotja de Pescadors
places.architect: OAB (Carlos Ferrater, Lucía Ferrater), Jesús Coll
places.why: The new fishermen's market on the Moll del Rellotge in the port of Barceloneta, winner of the Barcelona City Architecture Award 2024.

places.title: Park Güell
places.why: Gaudí's hillside garden city of mosaic benches, rough-stone viaducts and gingerbread pavilions overlooking the city.

photos.file: 028 El parc Güell i la Salut des del turó de la Rovira.JPG
photos.author: Enfo

places.title: Walden 7
places.why: A red labyrinth of 446 apartments around interlocking courtyards, bridges and vertical voids — Bofill's city in the air. Residential: view it from outside.

photos.author: No machine-readable author provided. Barkeno~commonswiki assumed (based on copyright claims).

places.title: La Fábrica
places.why: A cement factory turned by Bofill into his home and studio: concrete silos and ruins wrapped in cypresses and climbing plants.

places.title: Edifici Atalaya
places.architect: Federico Correa, Alfonso Milà, José Luis Sanz Magallón
places.why: A residential tower of stacked, set-back volumes in concrete and dark glass on the upper Diagonal — a landmark of Barcelona brutalism.

photos.file: 268 Avinguda Diagonal, 523-525 (Barcelona), edificis Atalaya i Naturgy.jpg
photos.author: Enric

places.title: Media-TIC
places.why: An office cube behind a skin of inflatable ETFE cushions that fill with nitrogen fog to shade the building in summer.

places.why: A white leaning mast with a curved ring whose shadow works as a sundial on the Olympic plaza.

places.title: Torre Colom
places.architect: Josep Anglada, Daniel Gelabert, Josep Ribas
places.why: One of the first skyscrapers of Barcelona, crowned by a projecting top floor, facing the Columbus monument.

photos.file: 005 Arts Santa Mònica i edifici Colón.jpg
photos.author: Enfo

places.title: Faculty of Economics, University of Barcelona
places.architect: Guillermo Giráldez, Pedro López Íñigo, Xavier Subías
places.why: A campus building of exposed concrete frames and brick panels on the Diagonal — the Catalan take on post-war brutalism.

places.title: Tres Xemeneies (Sant Adrià power station)
places.why: Three 200-metre concrete chimneys of a decommissioned power station on the shore — the landmark of the metropolitan coast.

places.title: Hospital Duran i Reynals
places.why: A brutalist slab built in the 1970s as a hotel and converted into a cancer hospital, with deep sculpted balconies.

places.title: Crypt of the Colònia Güell
places.why: Gaudí's laboratory for the Sagrada Família: a crypt of leaning basalt columns and brick vaults in a former textile workers' village.

places.title: Torre Mare Nostrum (Gas Natural HQ)
places.why: A glass tower with a huge cantilevered wing reaching out over the street — a collage of mirrored volumes by the sea.

places.title: Torre de Collserola
places.why: A needle-thin telecommunications tower held by cables on the ridge of Collserola, with a viewing deck over the city.

places.title: Jardí Botànic de Barcelona
places.architect: Carlos Ferrater, Josep Lluís Canosa, Bet Figueras
places.why: Mediterranean plants from five regions of the world on a triangulated grid of paths and concrete walls that follows the slope of Montjuïc.

places.title: Parc del Fòrum
places.architect: Martínez Lapeña & Torres (esplanade and pergola), Beth Galí (bathing area), FOA (Parc dels Auditoris)
places.why: The seafront of the 2004 Forum: a giant tilted photovoltaic pergola, a sheltered bathing area in the sea and landscaped dunes.

places.title: Parc de Diagonal Mar
places.why: A park of tube-like steel pergolas, ponds and gentle hills winding from the Diagonal toward the sea.

photos.file: 088 Parc de Diagonal Mar, pg. Taulat (Barcelona), al fons els edificis Illa del Mar.jpg

places.title: Superilla de Sant Antoni
places.why: Streets around the Sant Antoni market taken back from cars and turned into shaded squares with tables, play areas and trees.

places.title: Parc Central de Nou Barris
places.why: A large neighbourhood park of long ramps, water channels and green terraces that stitches together the hillside districts of Nou Barris.

places.title: Passeig de Sant Joan
places.why: A 19th-century boulevard redesigned with wide tree-lined walks, play areas and planted verges — a model for greening the Eixample.

shapes.name: Passeig de Sant Joan (Arc de Triomf to Verdaguer)

photos.file: Passeig de Sant Joan Barcelona Catalonia.JPG

places.title: Turó de la Rovira
places.architect: Imma Jansana, Conchita de la Villa, Robert de Paauw (landscaping)
places.why: Civil War anti-aircraft batteries on a hilltop, restored as a free lookout with one of the widest views over Barcelona.

photos.author: Enric

places.title: Plaça de les Glòries
places.architect: Agence Ter, Ana Coello, Meta Engineering
places.why: A former motorway junction turned into a large park and meadow over a road tunnel, between Torre Glòries, the Encants and the Design Museum.

photos.file: 055 Plaça de les Glòries Catalanes (Barcelona), amb el Museu del Disseny i la Torre Glòries.jpg
photos.author: Enric

places.title: Gothic Quarter and the Cathedral
places.why: The medieval core on Barcelona's Roman hill: narrow lanes and squares — Plaça del Rei, Plaça Sant Jaume, Plaça Reial, Sant Felip Neri — around the Gothic cathedral and its cloister.
places.note: The outline is the official el Gòtic district, which also takes in the Port Vell piers.

places.title: Santa Maria del Mar
places.why: The purest work of Catalan Gothic: a hall church of slender octagonal columns set wide apart, built in half a century by the people of the Ribera quarter.

photos.file: Barcelona-Ciutat Vella, toren van basilika de Santa Maria del Mar RI-51-0000421 IMG 3388 2026-08-28 16.20.jpg
photos.author: Michielverbeek

places.title: University of Barcelona — Historic Building
places.why: A neo-Romanesque university palace built around two arcaded cloisters and a botanical garden, with the gilded neo-Mudéjar Paranimf hall at its centre.

photos.file: Edifici històric de la Universitat de Barcelona 10.jpg
photos.author: Léna

places.title: Arc de Triomf and Passeig de Lluís Companys
places.why: A red-brick Neo-Mudéjar arch built as the gateway to the 1888 Universal Exposition, opening onto a wide palm-lined promenade that leads to the Ciutadella park.

photos.file: 043 Bombolles al pg. Lluís Companys (Barcelona), al fons el Palau de Justícia.jpg
photos.author: Enric

places.title: Tibidabo
places.why: The highest summit above the city, crowned by the Sagrat Cor church and a century-old amusement park, with the widest view over Barcelona and the sea.

photos.file: Temple del Sagrat Cor vist des de la Talaia del Tibidabo.JPG
photos.author: Jordiferrer

photos.file: Catalunya en Miniatura-Tibidabo - Vista posterior del Temple Expiatori del Sagrat Cor.JPG
photos.author: Jordiferrer

places.title: Seafront promenade: Barceloneta to Mar Bella
places.why: Four and a half kilometres of beaches and promenade opened up to the city for the 1992 Olympics, from the fishermen's quarter of Barceloneta past the Olympic Port towers to the quieter beaches of Poblenou.

places.title: Montjuïc: Palau Nacional, Magic Fountain and Castle
places.architect: Eugenio Cendoya, Enric Catà, Pere Domènech (Palau Nacional); Carles Buïgas (fountain)
places.why: The park-covered hill of the 1929 International Exposition: a grand axis of stairs and fountains from Plaça d'Espanya up to the Palau Nacional, with gardens, museums and the castle above the port.

photos.file: 007 Les Quatre Columnes i el Palau Nacional.jpg
photos.author: Enfo

places.title: La Rambla
places.why: The tree-lined promenade that runs 1.2 km from Plaça de Catalunya to the port, past the Liceu opera house and the Boqueria market; at its calmest early in the morning.

photos.file: 024 Barcelona des de l'edifici Colom, amb la Rambla i el Gòtic.jpg
photos.author: Enric

photos.file: 080 El pla de la Boqueria i la Rambla (Barcelona).jpg
photos.author: Enric

places.title: Passeig de Gràcia
places.architect: Ildefons Cerdà (Eixample plan); lamp-benches by Pere Falqués
places.why: The grand boulevard of the Eixample, lined with Modernista landmarks — Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller and Casa Lleó Morera on the Block of Discord, La Pedrera further up — and Falqués's tiled lamp-benches.

photos.file: 052 Edifici al pg. de Gràcia, 89 (Barcelona), cantonada c. Provença.jpg
photos.author: Enric

places.title: Parc de la Ciutadella
places.architect: Josep Fontserè (with the young Gaudí on the cascade)
places.why: The city's first great park, laid out on the site of a hated fortress and used for the 1888 Exposition: a monumental cascade, a boating lake, iron greenhouses and the Castell dels Tres Dragons.

photos.author: Enric

places.title: Mercat de la Boqueria
places.why: The city's most famous food market, under an iron roof with a stained-glass Modernista entrance arch on La Rambla.

places.title: Carrer de Montcada and the Museu Picasso
places.why: A narrow medieval street of Gothic merchant palaces with arcaded courtyards; five of them house the Museu Picasso.

places.title: Casa Amatller
places.why: A stepped Flemish-style gable in glazed tiles next to Casa Batlló, remodelled for a chocolate maker; the house keeps its original Modernista interiors.

photos.author: The original uploader was Argyriou at English Wikipedia .

places.title: Torre Bellesguard
places.why: Gaudí's neo-Gothic castle-house on the site of a medieval royal residence, in stone and brick with a slender cross-topped tower.

places.title: Gran Teatre del Liceu
places.architect: Miquel Garriga i Roca; rebuilt by Ignasi de Solà-Morales
places.why: The opera house on La Rambla: a sober facade in front of a gilded horseshoe auditorium in red velvet, rebuilt after the fire of 1994.

places.title: Casa de les Punxes
places.why: A whole Eixample block turned into a brick castle with six pointed towers, Nordic-Gothic gables and tiled panels.

places.why: The oldest garden in the city: neoclassical terraces with a cypress maze and pavilions, and a romantic garden added in the 19th century.
